Crop: Sugarcane (ಕಬ್ಬು / Saccharum officinarum L. Poaceae) | Topic: Intercropping Details
Title: ಮಿಶ್ರ ಬೆಳೆ (Intercropping)
Content: ಕಬ್ಬಿನ ಜೊತೆ ಮಿಶ್ರ ಬೆಳೆ ಮಾಡುವುದರಿಂದ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಆದಾಯ ಬರುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಮಣ್ಣಿನ ಫಲವತ್ತತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ. ಸೂಕ್ತ ಮಿಶ್ರ ಬೆಳೆಗಳೆಂದರೆ ಈರುಳ್ಳಿ, ಆಲೂಗೆಡ್ಡೆ, ಕೊತ್ತಂಬರಿ, ಮೆಂತ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ಅವರೆಕಾಳು. ಕಬ್ಬಿನ ಆರಂಭಿಕ 3 ತಿಂಗಳು ಮಿಶ್ರ ಬೆಳೆ ಬೆಳೆಯಲು ಸೂಕ್ತ ಸಮಯ. ದ್ವಿದಳ ಧಾನ್ಯ ಬೆಳೆ ಮಿಶ್ರ ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಮಣ್ಣಿನ ಸಾರಜನಕ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ. ಮಿಶ್ರ ಬೆಳೆ ಕಬ್ಬಿನ ಮುಖ್ಯ ಬೆಳೆಗೆ ಸ್ಪರ್ಧೆ ನೀಡಬಾರದು.
Suitable Intercrops:
  - ಈರುಳ್ಳಿ (Onion)
  - ಆಲೂಗೆಡ್ಡೆ (Potato)
  - ಕೊತ್ತಂಬರಿ (Coriander)
  - ಮೆಂತ್ಯ (Fenugreek)
  - ಅವರೆಕಾಳು (Cowpea)
Benefits:
  Income: Extra ₹5,000-10,000 per acre
  Soil: Legumes fix nitrogen in the soil.
Timing: First 3 months

Crop: Sugarcane (ಕಬ್ಬು / Saccharum officinarum L. Poaceae) | Topic: Weather And Seasonal Advice
Title: ಹವಾಮಾನ ಮತ್ತು ಋತು ಸಲಹೆ
Optimal Range: 21-35°C with bright sunshine.
Seasonal Risks:
  Monsoon: Drainage is crucial; risk of root rot.
  Summer: Increase irrigation intervals; use trash mulch.
  Winter: Growth slows down below 12°C.
  Hailstorm: Spray fungicide immediately if hailstorms occur.
Annual Rainfall Needed: 1200-1500 mm

Seed Treatment:
  Method: Disease Protection (Sett Dipping)
  Details: Dip the sugarcane setts in a 0.1% Carbendazim 50 WP solution (1 g/L water) for 10-15 minutes before planting to prevent Pineapple disease (ಅನಾನಸ್ ರೋಗ) and soil-borne fungal infections.

  Method: Hot Water Treatment (Yellow Leaf/Smut Protection)
  Details: Treat setts in moist hot air/water at 52°C for 1 hour to eliminate internal viruses and smut before nursery planting.

Crop: Sugarcane (ಕಬ್ಬು / Saccharum officinarum L. Poaceae) | Topic: Intercultivation And Cropping Systems
Earthing Up: Done after last top dressing of nitrogen and after each top dressing to give support to the main plant and tillers.
Wrapping And Propping: Wrapping: Tying stalks of same clump with lower/dried leaves. Propping: Giving support with bamboo or tying wrapped canes to adjacent rows.
Intercropping: French bean & soybean (Variety: KB-79) or pulse/legumes.
Sequenced Crops: Potato, Rice, Wheat, Cotton, Sorghum, Chickpea, Groundnut.

Name: Pineapple Disease / Sett Rot (ಅನಾನಸ್ ರೋಗ)
Recommendations:

  Chemical Kannada: ಕಾರ್ಬೆಂಡೈಜಿಮ್ 50 ಡಬ್ಲ್ಯೂ.ಪಿ

Crop: Sugarcane (ಕಬ್ಬು / Saccharum officinarum L. Poaceae) | Topic: General Information
Significance: World's most important sugar crop; plays a vital role in Indian economy. Largest processing industry in India next to cotton.
Employment: Employs nearly 35 million growers & 3,30,000 skilled personnel.
Industry Stats: About 550 sugar factories in India with 135 milling days.
Origin: North-East India & New Guinea
Distribution Global: India, Brazil, Cuba, Mexico, Pakistan, China, Philippines, Thailand
Distribution India: UP, TN, Maharashtra, Karnataka. UP stands first with 50% area and 40% production. TN stands first in yield.

Crop: Sugarcane (ಕಬ್ಬು / Saccharum officinarum L. Poaceae) | Topic: Seed Rate
Acre Basis:
  Line Sowing: 10,000 to 12,000 three-budded setts/acre
  Notes: Select disease-free setts from an 8-10 month old healthy nursery crop. For wide row spacing, 7,000-8,000 setts are sufficient.
Hectare Basis:
  Standard: 25,000-30,000 setts (5-7 t) per hectare
  Notes: Use 3 eye bud setts.

Crop: Sugarcane (ಕಬ್ಬು / Saccharum officinarum L. Poaceae) | Topic: Harvesting And Seed Production
Maturity Indicators: 12-14 months after planting. Withered lower leaves & few green leaves at top, metallic sound of stem, hand refractometer reading (Brix) between 18-20.
Harvesting Method: Manual cutting at ground level (ನೆಲಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಕತ್ತರಿಸುವುದು). Detrashing and cutting the green top. Transport to factory within 24 hours to prevent sucrose loss.
Seed Cane Production: Seed cane should be free from pests/diseases, high in moisture, rich in invert sugars/soluble nitrogen. Top 2/3rd portion is suitable due to apical dominance.

Crop: Sugarcane (ಕಬ್ಬು / Saccharum officinarum L. Poaceae) | Topic: Climate And Soil
Title Kannada: ಮಣ್ಣಿನ ತಯಾರಿ ಮತ್ತು ಭೂ ನಿರ್ವಹಣೆ
Climate: Tropical to subtropical. Optimum temperature: 21-35°C (Growth arrests if <20°C or >50°C). Cold stress below 12°C.
Rainfall: Well distributed annual rainfall of 750-1200 mm is optimum. Total water requirement: 1200-1500 mm.
Sunshine: Bright sunshine leads to thicker, shorter stems and broader greener leaves. Low sunshine leads to slender, long stems with narrow yellowish leaves.
Day Length: Short day length decreases tillers and tonnage. Long day produces more dry matter.
Soil Requirements:
  Soil Type: Deep red soil, Black soil; well-drained loamy soils are ideal (ಆಳವಾದ ಕೆಂಪು ಮಣ್ಣು, ಕಪ್ಪು ಮಣ್ಣು).
  Soil Ph: 6.0 to 7.5 (Optimum)
  Drainage: Essential — water should not stagnate (ಅತ್ಯಗತ್ಯ — ನೀರು ನಿಲ್ಲಬಾರದು)
  Notes: Saline and alkaline soils are not suitable.

Crop: Sugarcane (ಕಬ್ಬು / Saccharum officinarum L. Poaceae) | Topic: Specialty Canes And Sugars
Fibre Cane:
  Description: Bred for fibre or bagasse for paper industries. Less sugar, high biomass, more tillers.
  Varieties: S. robustum varieties Co-421, Co-423, Co-426
Energy Cane:
  Description: Bred for high molasses production for bio-fuel. Grown with closer spacing & high nitrogen. High biomass and total sugars.
  Varieties: PR-980, CP 65-357 (Yields 4000-6000 L alcohol/ha)
Artificial Sugars:
  Description: Low calorie alternatives for health/lifestyle.
  Types:
    - Saccharin (300x sweeter, bitter aftertaste)
    - Aspartame (180x sweeter)
    - Acesulfame-K (110x sweeter)
    - Hydrogenated glucose syrup
    - Isomalt
    - Xylitol
    - High Fructose Corn Syrup (HFCS) - replaces sugar up to 10% in soft drinks.

Crop: Sugarcane (ಕಬ್ಬು / Saccharum officinarum L. Poaceae) | Topic: Botanical Classification
Cultivated Species:
  Species: Saccharum officinarum
  Characteristics: Thick and juicy cane, good for chewing, indigenous to New Guinea. High sugar %, low fibre, high tonnage. Generally resistant to smut but susceptible to red rot. Tropical areas.
  Type: Noble cane

  Species: Saccharum sinense
  Characteristics: Indigenous to N-E India, long thin stalks, broad leaves, low/medium sucrose, early maturity. Zig-zag internodes with prominent nodes.

  Species: Saccharum barbery
  Characteristics: Indigenous to N-E India, short thin stalks, narrow leaves, low/medium sucrose, early maturing.

Wild Species:
  - Saccharum spontaneum
  - Saccharum robustum

Crop: Sugarcane (ಕಬ್ಬು / Saccharum officinarum L. Poaceae) | Topic: Industrial Processing And Byproducts
Standard Yield: 100t of cane produces 10t sugar + 4t molasses + 3t filter mud + 0.3t ash + 30t bagasse
Bagasse: Used as fuel, for making fibre boards and paper (7t bagasse = 1t paper).
Molasses: Used in distilleries for ethyl alcohol (ethanol), blended with petrol (Gasohol). Used for oxalic, maleic, and citric acid, Rum, and livestock feed additive.
Press Mud: Rich in organic 'C', 'P', & 'S'; used in vermicomposting as manure.
Green Tops: Good sources of fodder.
Co Generation: A plant of 2500 TCD generates 7-8 MW surplus power.

Crop: Sugarcane (ಕಬ್ಬು / Saccharum officinarum L. Poaceae) | Topic: Botany And Growth
Plant Type: Perennial grass growing in tropical regions.
Morphology: 3-4 m height, tillering, unbranching stalk (cane). Stalk has distinct nodes and internodes coated with waxy material. Eye bud at each node protected by leaf sheath.
Tillering: Produces 20-40 tillers per cane from below soil surface.
Inflorescence: Called 'arrow', has male and female parts. Produced at 10-12 months (qualitative short day plant).
Root System:
  Sett Roots: Temporary roots from root primordia at the base of every cane joint; provide initial moisture and nutrients.
  Shoot Roots: Permanent, thick fleshy white roots from lower nodes of the primary shoot; provide anchorage.
Flowering Disadvantages: Reduces quality (1% Sucrose loss), pithy canes, loss of apical dominance, development of water shoots, shorter leaf blade, low yield (25% loss), high fibre, reduced juice extraction.

Definition: Allowing the stubble to regrow after the harvest of the main crop.
Advantages: Shorter crop cycle, reduces seed cost (25-30%), better utilization of climate.
Disadvantages: Lower yields due to poor sprouting/soil compaction, build-up of pests/diseases, early run-out of commercial varieties.
Management Practices:
  Trash Burning: Advised if plant crop is infested with scales/mealy bugs, termites, rodents, or excess moisture affecting sprouting.
  Stubble Shaving: Cutting protruding stubbles to ground level with a spade to facilitate healthy underground bud sprouting and deep root system.
  Off Barring: Breaking/cutting ridges on either side to loosen soil between rows, reducing compaction and aiding root development.
  Gap Filling: Crucial if gaps >20%. Done using pre-germinated single eye bud setts or excess sprouts. Fill gaps with new seedlings.

  Details: Square pits 40-60 cm dug at 90 cm apart. Trenches dug after every 3 rows to store water. Suitable for low rainfall areas. Two setts planted per pit (>5 cm depth).
